whenToUse: People skim a long list quickly, such as a playlist.
Kiosks or preview screens scrolled by dragging with a mouse.
It must feel the same as the browser's own scrolling.
whenNotToUse: The browser's default scrolling is enough (don't build your own).
Lists that must stop at exact positions (use scroll snap).
People who turned on reduced motion.

alternatives.name: Scroll Bounce
alternatives.reason: Showing that the end was reached.

accessibility: The scroll area has a tabIndex and a name, so it can be scrolled with the keyboard.
With reduced motion, it doesn't glide after release.
Touch and wheel use the browser's default behavior.
overscroll-behavior: contain keeps the page from moving along at the end.
